'''HCL Group''' is an Indian [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] that operates across sectors including [[information technology]] services, [[healthcare]], [[technology]] [[distribution]], and [[education technology]].<ref name="u025">{{cite web |date=2014-02-06 |title=HCL Corporation forays into healthcare; to invest Rs 1,000 crore |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/healthcare/hcl-corporation-forays-into-healthcare-to-invest-rs-1000-crore/articleshow/29958600.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref>
Its largest subsidiary, [[HCLTech]], provides IT [[consulting]] and engineering services to enterprises in industries including [[financial services]], [[manufacturing]], [[telecommunications]], and technology.<ref name="q759">{{cite web |last1=Rag |first1=Ajay |last2=Rajan |first2=Jessica |date=2024-03-05 |title=HCL Group: HCL Group invests Rs 166 crore in edtech firm Educational Initiatives |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/funding/hcl-group-invests-rs-166-crore-in-edtech-firm-education-initiatives/articleshow/108214335.cms |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref>

==History==
===Founding and early years=== 
HCL started as a company focused on the development of [[BBC Micro|microcomputer systems]] and [[electronic computing]] products. It was founded in 1976 as Hindustan Computers Limited (HCL) by [[Shiv Nadar]] along with seven other founders, formerly associated with [[Delhi Cloth & General Mills]] (DCM).<ref name="q045">{{cite web |date=2007-11-28 |title=Tracing Arjun Malhotra’s journey from HCL to Headstrong |url=https://www.livemint.com/Industry/2UotJbHm3uS6bHnuF38UpN/Web-Exclusive-Tracing-Arjun-Malhotra8217s-journey-from-H.html |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=mint}}</ref>

In 1978, HCL introduced the Micro 2200, regarded as one of the earliest [[Microcomputer|microcomputers]] designed and manufactured in [[India]]. During the 1980s, the company expanded its product portfolio to include enterprise computing systems and personal computers.<ref name="u459">{{cite web |date=2007-06-09 |title=The amazing story of the birth of HCL |url=https://www.rediff.com/business/special/bspec1/20070609.htm |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Rediff}}</ref>

In 1981, HCL participated in the establishment of NIIT as a technology education institution, which was later spun off as an independent organization.<ref name="v622">{{cite web |last=Nair |first=Radhika P |date=2011-11-18 |title='NIIT pioneered IT education in India' |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/india-emerging/niit-pioneered-it-education-inhttps://economictimes.indiatimes.com/india-emerging/niit-pioneered-it-education-in-india/articleshow/10775340.cms?from=mdr-india/articleshow/10775340.cms?from=mdrhttps://economictimes.indiatimes.com/india-emerging/niit-pioneered-it-education-in-india/articleshow/10775340.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref><ref name="o682">{{cite web |date=2011-05-03 |title=The man behind NIIT's success |url=https://www.rediff.com/business/slide-show/slide-show-1-the-man-behind-niits-success/20110503.htm |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Rediff}}</ref>

===Expansion and global partnerships===

During the early 1990s, HCL expanded its business through international partnerships and distribution agreements. In 1991, the group formed a joint venture with [[Hewlett-Packard]] to distribute computing products and services in India.<ref name="q817">{{cite web |last=Khanna |first=Sundeep |date=2013-09-09 |title=Merger with Hewlett-Packard to transform HCL |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/economy/story/19911015-merger-with-hewlett-packard-to-transform-hcl-814937-1991-10-14 |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=India Today}}</ref>

In 1994, the company expanded its distribution operations through partnerships with telecommunications companies including [[Nokia]] and [[Ericsson]].<ref name="c878">{{cite web |last=Chowdhry |first=Ajai |date=2023-04-14 |title=How HCL-Nokia partnership made mobile phones affordable for Indians in the 1990s |url=https://theprint.in/pageturner/excerpt/how-hcl-nokia-partnership-made-mobile-phones-affordable-for-indians-in-the-1990s/1517817/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=ThePrint}}</ref>

As the [[Global Technology Associates|global technology]] industry increasingly shifted toward software services and outsourcing, HCL began restructuring its business operations. HCL Technologies was established as a separate entity focused on software development and IT services, while HCL Infosystems was reorganized to manage hardware manufacturing, systems integration, and domestic market operations. 

HCL Technologies expanded its global delivery operations and completed an [[initial public offering]] in 2000.<ref name="q431">{{cite web |author=The Times of India |date=2025-01-18 |title=25 years of HCLTech IPO: IT major gave over 1300% return since market debut |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/25-years-of-hcltech-ipo-it-major-gave-over-1300-return-since-market-debut/articleshow/117359753.cms |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Times of India}}</ref>

===Shift from hardware to IT services===
During the 2000s, HCL Technologies expanded internationally and became one of India's major IT services companies, providing application development, infrastructure services, and engineering solutions to enterprise clients.<ref name="k924">{{cite web |last=Bhan |first=Shereen |date=2024-10-29 |title=HCLTech looks to expand global footprint by focusing on AI, local partnerships |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/technology/exclusive-hcltech-looks-to-expand-global-footprint-by-focusing-on-ai-local-partnerships-19501051.htm |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=CNBCTV18}}</ref><ref name="n730">{{cite web |last=Desk Report |first=Tech Observer |date=2021-05-20 |title=HCL looks to expand UK operations, pump up UK team size to support 50 international clients |url=https://techobserver.in/news/enterprise-it/hcl-looks-to-expand-uk-operations-pump-up-uk-team-size-to-support-50-international-clients-249783/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Tech Observer Magazine}}</ref><ref name="d005">{{cite web |date=2019-12-16 |title=HCL Technologies expands presence in Lithuania |url=https://indbiz.gov.in/hcl-technologies-expands-presence-in-lithuania/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=IndBiz}}</ref>

During the same period, the group's hardware manufacturing business declined as the global personal computer market changed, and competition from international manufacturers increased. HCL Infosystems discontinued the manufacturing of HCL-branded personal computers in 2013 and shifted its focus toward technology distribution and services.<ref name="v522">{{cite web |date=2018-03-12 |title=HCL Infosystems to exit PC manufacturing business |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/hcl-infosystems-to-exit-pc-manufacturing-business/article64095976.ece |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=BusinessLine}}</ref><ref name="x671">{{cite web |date=2013-11-17 |title=HCL Infosystems to phase-off manufacturing business |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/hardware/hcl-infosystems-to-phase-off-manufacturing-business/articleshow/25937041.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref><ref name="j313">{{cite web |last=News report |first=Web Desk |date=2013-11-16 |title=HCL to down shutters on PC business |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/hcl-to-down-shutters-on-pc-business-113111500984_1.html |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Business Standard}}</ref>

===Diversification and new initiatives===
In recent years, HCL Group has expanded into sectors including [[Health care|healthcare]] services, [[Educational technology|education technology]], and [[semiconductor]] manufacturing.<ref name="o486">{{cite web |last1=Rag |first1=Ajay |last2=Rajan |first2=Jessica |date=2024-03-05 |title=HCL Group: HCL Group invests Rs 166 crore in edtech firm Educational Initiatives |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/funding/hcl-group-invests-rs-166-crore-in-edtech-firm-education-initiatives/articleshow/108214335.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref><ref name="o485">{{cite web |last=Rajput |first=Vinod |date=2026-02-12 |title=HCL-Foxconn semiconductor manufacturing unit's foundation event on Feb 21: Yeida |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/noida-news/hclfoxconn-semiconductor-manufacturing-unit-s-foundation-event-on-feb-21yeida-101770834784145.html#google_vignette |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=Hindustan Times}}</ref>

The group has invested in technology education and skills development companies including [[GUVI]], a digital learning platform providing [[Computer programming|programming]] and [[technical education]] in multiple Indian languages.<ref name="u642">{{cite web |date=2026-04-14 |title=HCL acquires stake in GUVI; plans to skills tech professionals in India, abroad |url=https://www.vccircle.com/hclacquires-stake-in-guvi-plans-to-skills-tech-professionals-in-india-abroad |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=VCCircle}}</ref><ref name="m552">{{cite web |date=2022-09-29 |title=HCL Group acquires majority stake in vernacular edtech platform GUVI- Moneycontrol.com |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/hcl-group-acquires-majority-stake-in-vernacular-edtech-platform-guvi-9250221.html |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Moneycontrol}}</ref>

In 2025, [[Prudential plc]] announced plans to establish a standalone health insurance joint venture in India with Vama Sundari Investments, a promoter entity of HCL Group - with Prudential holding a 70% stake.<ref name="z288">{{cite web |last=Bureau Report |first=BL Mumbai |date=2025-03-20 |title=Prudential plc, HCL Group firm form JV for health insurance foray |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/prudential-plc-hcl-group-firm-form-jv-for-health-insurance-foray/article69352075.ece |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=BusinessLine}}</ref>

In 2025, HCL Group entered a 60:40 semiconductor joint venture with [[Foxconn]] named India Chip Private Limited.<ref name="n615">{{cite web |date=2026-01-15 |title=Foxconn-HCL name semiconductor JV as India Chip Private Limited |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/foxconn-hcl-name-semiconductor-jv-as-india-chip-private-limited/article70512142.ece |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=BusinessLine}}</ref><ref name="z089">{{cite web |date=2026-01-14 |title=Foxconn, HCL Group name semiconductor JV as India Chip Pvt Ltd |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/foxconn-hcl-group-name-semiconductor-jv-as-india-chip-pvt-ltd/articleshow/126530915.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref> The [[Government of India]] approved a ₹3,706 crore Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility in Jewar, [[Uttar Pradesh]], under the India Semiconductor Mission.<ref name="h641">{{cite web |author=The Hindu Bureau |date=2025-05-14 |title=Union Cabinet approves ₹3,706 crore HCL-Foxconn semiconductor joint venture; plant to be set up at Jewar |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/union-cabinet-approves-3706-crore-hcl-foxconn-semiconductor-joint-venture-plant-to-be-set-up-at-jewar/article69574825.ece |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Hindu}}</ref><ref name="f295">{{cite web |last=Rajput |first=Vinod |date=2026-02-12 |title=HCL-Foxconn semiconductor manufacturing unit's foundation event on Feb 21: Yeida |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/noida-news/hclfoxconn-semiconductor-manufacturing-unit-s-foundation-event-on-feb-21yeida-101770834784145.html |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=Hindustan Times}}</ref>

== Businesses ==
HCL Group operates through several companies across technology services, [[Health care|healthcare]], and [[technology]] distribution. 

===HCLTech===
HCLTech is the group's largest company and operates as a global provider of IT services and engineering solutions. The company offers services including [[application development]], [[cloud computing]], [[Computer security|cybersecurity]], [[Infrastructure Management service|infrastructure management]], and [[Engineering|engineering services]] for enterprise clients across multiple industries.<ref name="q577">{{cite web |date=2024-04-01 |title=HCL Technologies Information |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/hcl-technologies-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-4291.cms |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref><ref name="q431"/>
===HCL Infosystems===
HCL Infosystems historically managed the group's hardware manufacturing and personal computer business in India. After discontinuing PC manufacturing in 2013, the company transitioned toward technology distribution, systems integration, and services.<ref name="k338">{{cite web |date=2013-01-16 |title=HCL Info hives off 3 businesses into separate firms |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/hcl-info-hives-off-3-businesses-into-separate-firms/article4309947.ece |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Hindu}}</ref><ref name="y999">{{cite web |last=Archives |first=FP |date=2013-11-19 |title=It's the end of PC manufacturing business for HCL Infosystems |url=https://www.firstpost.com/business/its-the-end-of-pc-manufacturing-business-for-hcl-infosystems-1238117.html |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Firstpost}}</ref>

===HCL Healthcare===
HCL Healthcare provides clinical care and workplace health services in India. The business operates a network of clinics and health centers offering preventive healthcare, diagnostics, and occupational health services.<ref name="w815">{{cite web |last=Barkha Mathur |first=New Delhi |date=2025-05-20 |title=Most Indian corporate employees face emotional distress, HCL Healthcare finds |url=https://www.business-standard.com/health/emotional-health-hcl-report-indian-corporates-anxiety-stress-burnout-125052000093_1.html |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Business Standard}}</ref>

HCL Group is an Indian multinational conglomerate that operates across sectors including information technology services, healthcare, technology distribution, and education technology.
Its largest subsidiary, HCLTech, provides IT consulting and engineering services to enterprises in industries including financial services, manufacturing, telecommunications, and technology.
